# Real-life Data

## Ideal vs Reality

| Expected | Reality |
|----------|---------|
| Equidistant | Irregular activity |
| Smooth | Noisy |
| Continuous | Possible jumps |
| Single price | Bid / Ask / Mid |

## Data processing

| Approach | Usage | Limitation |
|----------|-------|------------|
| **Discretisation** | 99,9% of cases | Information lost between ticks |
| **Interpolation** | Rare | Strong assumptions, arbitrary physical time |

# Moving Averages

## Comparison of the three operators

| | **SMA** | **WMA** | **EMA** |
|---|---|---|---|
| Weights | Equal $\frac{1}{n}$ | Linearly increasing | Exponential decay |
| Memory | $n$ observations | $n$ observations | 1 value only |
| Update | Simple | Complex | Very simple |
| Infinite memory | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |

## Key formulas

**SMA** — window $n$ :

$$\text{SMA}(t) = \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=0}^{n-1} X_{t-i}$$

Update : $\text{SMA}(t+1) = \text{SMA}(t) - \dfrac{X_{t-n+1}}{n} + \dfrac{X_{t+1}}{n}$

**WMA** — denominator $= \dfrac{n(n+1)}{2}$ :

$$\text{WMA}(t) = \frac{\sum_{i=1}^{n} i \cdot X_{t-n+i}}{\frac{n(n+1)}{2}}$$

**EMA** — recursive form (**central formula**) :

$$\boxed{\text{EMA}(t) = \alpha \cdot X_t + (1-\alpha) \cdot \text{EMA}(t-1)}$$

## Choice of $\alpha$ for the EMA

| Method | Formula | Remark |
|---------|---------|--------|
| SMA($n$) equivalence | $\alpha = \dfrac{2}{n+1}$ | Same average age, **not identical** |
| Residual impact $\epsilon_k$ after $k$ steps | $\alpha = 1 - e^{\log(\epsilon_k)/k}$ | Ex : $k=100$, $\epsilon=1\%$ $\Rightarrow \alpha=0{,}045$ |

## Initialisation (Initial Conditions)

- $\text{EMA}(1) = X_1$ — simple, possible initial bias
- $\text{EMA}(n) = \text{SMA}(n)$ — more robust

⚠️ **Warm-up period required** — the smaller $\alpha$, the longer it is.

## Pitfalls to avoid

- ⚠️ $\alpha = \frac{2}{n+1}$ **≠** SMA($n$) — only the average age is equivalent
- ⚠️ The stronger the smoothing → the greater the **time lag** — **inevitable**
- ⚠️ Small $\alpha$ = strong smoothing = long lag ; large $\alpha$ = reactive = little smoothing

## Asynchronous EMA (irregular data)

$$\text{EMA}(\tau; x)(t_n) = \mu \cdot \text{EMA}(t_{n-1}) + (\nu - \mu) \cdot x_{n-1} + (1-\nu) \cdot x_n$$

| Parameter | Definition |
|-----------|-----------|
| $\alpha = (t_n - t_{n-1})/\tau$ | Normalised elapsed time |
| $\mu = e^{-\alpha}$ | Exponential decay |
| $\nu = (1-\mu)/\alpha$ | Interpolation between $x_{n-1}$ and $x_n$ |

# Intrinsic Time

## Why go beyond physical time?

- Important events can occur **between** two observations
- Observation start **arbitrary** (midnight, 5am...)
- Physical time **insensitive** to actual market activity

💡 Solution : let the **market dictate its own rhythm**

## Fundamental concepts

| Term | Definition |
|------|-----------|
| **DC** (Directional Change) | Price reversal ≥ threshold $\delta$ since last extreme |
| **OS** (Overshoot) | Movement beyond the DC until next reversal |
| **TM** (Total Move) | $\text{TM} = \text{DC} + \text{OS}$ |
| **$\delta$** | Detection threshold — controls temporal granularity |

## Properties of intrinsic time

- $\delta$ small → many DCs → **fast** time (volatile market)
- $\delta$ large → few DCs → **slow** time (calm market)
- Number of DCs / physical time ∝ **volatility**
- Length of OS ∝ **liquidity**

## DC detection algorithm

```
mode = "up", x_ext = first price, δ fixed

For each price x :
  If mode = "up" :
    If x < x_ext  →  x_ext = x
    If (x_ext - x) / x_ext ≥ δ  →  DC up detected, x_ext = x, mode = "down"

  If mode = "down" :
    If x > x_ext  →  x_ext = x
    If (x - x_ext) / x_ext ≥ δ  →  DC down detected, x_ext = x, mode = "up"
```

⚠️ The initial mode is **arbitrary** — the algorithm converges quickly.

## Scaling Laws

Empirical relations linking intrinsic time and physical time :

| Law | Formula |
|-----|---------|
| Price move vs time | $\langle \Delta x \rangle \sim \Delta t^{\alpha}$ |
| Average duration of a DC | $\langle \Delta t_\text{dc} \rangle \sim (\delta/c)^{\alpha}$ |
| Number of ticks vs $\delta$ | Decreasing power law |

🧠 **20 scaling laws** identified on 13 FX currency pairs — **universal and stable**.

# Global summary

| Concept | Keyword | Formula / Rule |
|---------|---------|----------------|
| SMA | Equal-weighted | $\frac{1}{n}\sum X_i$ |
| WMA | Linear | Weights $\propto$ recency |
| EMA | Exponential | $\alpha X_t + (1-\alpha)\text{EMA}(t-1)$ |
| Lag | Inevitable | $\uparrow n$ or $\downarrow \alpha$ $\Rightarrow$ $\uparrow$ lag |
| DC | Key event | Reversal $\geq \delta$ |
| Intrinsic time | Adaptive | Triggered by prices, not time |
| Scaling laws | Universal | Power law between DC and physical time |
